member.name: T:WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestOptions.HttpEngineLogCallback
member.summary: This property represents the delegate signature for the optional callback method that receives log messages from the HTTP Request engine to which this instance is attached. The callback method is expected to handle the log message appropriately, such as by writing it to a log file, displaying it in a console, or sending it to a logging service. The additional parameters provide context about the source of the log message, including the member name, source file path, and line number where the log message was generated. This information can be useful for debugging and tracing the flow of execution in the HTTP engine, allowing developers to identify the specific location in the code where the log message originated. The use of CallerMemberName, CallerFilePath, and CallerLineNumber attributes allows the HTTP engine to automatically capture this contextual information without requiring the caller to explicitly provide it, making it easier to implement logging throughout the codebase. Overall, this delegate provides a flexible and powerful mechanism for logging messages from the HTTP engine while also capturing important contextual information for debugging purposes.

param.name: pstrLogMessage
param.para: This string represents the log message generated by the HTTP engine. The content of the message can vary widely depending on the specific events and actions taking place within the engine, such as the initiation of a request, the receipt of a response, the occurrence of an error, or any other significant event that the engine deems worthy of logging. The message can include details about the request being processed, the response received, any exceptions encountered, or any other relevant information that can help developers under- stand the behavior of the HTTP engine and diagnose issues that may arise during its operation.

The log message can be formatted in a way that is consistent with the logging conventions used throughout the codebase, and may include timestamps, log levels, or other metadata to provide additional context for the message. Overall, the log message parameter serves as a crucial means of communication between the HTTP engine and the logging system, allowing developers to gain insights into the inner workings of the engine and troubleshoot any issues that may arise during its execution.
All messages begin with a prefix that identifies the call site of the constructor or other method that reported it, so that log entries can be easily traced back to their origin.

The additional parameters, including memberName (), sourceFilePath (), and sourceLineNumber (), provide valuable context about the source of the log message. The memberName parameter indicates the name of the method or property where the log message was generated within the HTTP engine, allowing developers to pinpoint the specific location in the code that is responsible for the log message. The sourceFilePath parameter provides the file path of the source code file where the log message originated, which can be helpful for navigating to the relevant code when investigating issues. The sourceLineNumber parameter indicates the line number within the source code file where the log message was generated, providing precise information about the location where the message originated. Together, these parameters enable developers to quickly and efficiently trace the flow of execution within the HTTP engine and identify any potential issues or areas for improvement based on the logged messages.

member.name: P:WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestOptions.RetryDelay
member.summary: This read-only integer property specifies the delay, in seconds, between retry attempts for a request that fails due to a transient error. The default value is 10, which means that the HTTP engine will wait for 10 seconds before attempting to retry a failed request. This parameter allows developers to control the timing of retry attempts, providing a mechanism for introducing a delay between retries to avoid overwhelming the server or network with rapid-fire requests. By adjusting the retry delay, developers can optimize the balance between retrying failed requests and avoiding excessive delays in the overall request processing.

member.name: P:WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestOptions.RetryLimit
member.summary: This read-only integer property specifies the maximum number of times to retry a request that fails due to a transient error, such as a network issue or a server error. The default value is 10, which means that the HTTP engine will attempt to retry a failed request up to 10 times before giving up and returning an error to the caller. This parameter allows developers to control the behavior of the HTTP engine in the face of transient errors, providing a mechanism for automatically retrying requests that may succeed on subsequent attempts.

member.name: P:WizardWrx.HTTP.RequestOptions.Timeout
member.summary:
This integer specifies the Timeout in seconds.
The default value is 100,000 milliseconds (100 seconds). The documentation for HttpClient.Timeout states that the default value is 100 seconds, and that the property is of type TimeSpan.
When unitialized, the Timeout property behaves as if it had been set to the default value of 100 seconds, which is equivalent to 100,000 milliseconds.
Though the Timeout property supports setting an infinite timeout by setting the property value to InfiniteTimeSpan, we do not support that feature in this library, as it is generally not advisable to allow requests to hang indefinitely.
